# Memory-Residuals Data Faithfulness Audit
*2026-05-08, autogenerated by audit subagent*

> **Scope.** Read-only audit of three sibling repos
> (`memory_residuals/`, `memory_residuals_data/`,
> `data_labeler_testing_env/`) against the user's question
> *"is the data the writers produce structurally compatible
> with what the architecture expects, and in particular —
> are callbacks being produced or are sessions accidentally
> self-contained?"*. No code in any of the three repos was
> modified; only this audit file was written.

---

## Executive Summary

**The current writer-produced data is NOT in shape to train the
memory-residual architecture as designed, and the dominant failure
mode is not callback density — it is that the writer→trainer
pipeline does not exist at all.** The architecture's `ChainCorpus`
loader (`src/train_chain.py:963-1047`) reads pre-tokenised
`.pt` blobs whose required fields include `chain_callback_position`,
`chain_evidence_positions`, and `session_callback_mask`; the
manifest of training corpora actually consumed in May 2026
(`paper_artifacts/chains/omni_memory_train_s512_manifest.json`) lists
LongMemEval, MSC, synthetic persona-callback, and synthetic random
codes — and zero references to anything in
`data_labeler_testing_env/presets/`. Whatever the writer portal
produces today is consumed by a different downstream system (the
`server.exe` chatbot in the labeler env), not by the memres
trainer. Any claim that the writers "are or are not producing
trainable data" is therefore presupposing a converter that no one
has written.

That said, the user's secondary worry — *"is the data
accidentally self-contained?"* — is largely confirmed. Even if a
converter were built tomorrow with sensible defaults (one Day = one
session, contiguous Day 1..N = one chain), the writer-side
pipeline is missing **four** of the six fields the trainer's
recipe leans on: `session_callback_mask` (the answer-span supervision
that delivered the +1.32-nat headline), `chain_callback_position`
(the LME-style "this session is the question"),
`chain_evidence_positions` (the LME-style "answer text lives in
session N"), and `session_role` (filler/evidence/callback tags).
None of these are recoverable from the writer JSON without an
LLM-grade post-hoc annotator. With no callback annotation, the
trainer's load-bearing flags (`--callback_loss_weight`,
`--curriculum_evidence_bias`, `--callback_window_bias`) all
silently fall back to uniform-NLL, and Prior #11 of `runs.md` is
pretty explicit: "callback annotation density on the bulk of
training chains is the dominant collapse cause" (v24c, going
negative when only 7% of chains are callback-supervised).

The user's specific framing — *"telling writers to add callbacks
is a teaching problem"* — is the right diagnosis. There IS a
callback signal in the highest-quality multi-day passed sequences
(e.g. user_34 Day2 → "昨天和你说的那个稳定臂", Day9 → "伯克利下周
会把新的控制板寄过来" recalling a Day 1 fact). It just isn't
*labelled* anywhere, isn't *rewarded* by the audit rubric, and
isn't *prompted* anywhere in the writer UI surface. Recommendations
for the teaching layer are in §"Teaching-side recommendations"
below; the load-bearing one is the hidden `reasoning_chain` field,
which the rubric calls a "blocker" if absent and which is *missing
from 99.74% of all 775 Kurisu CN files on disk* (2 / 775 have any
content there, and one of those two is the rubric's own example
fixture).

## What the Architecture Expects

Read end-to-end from `src/train_chain.py` and the corpus builders
in `tools/`. The architecture's input contract is a single PyTorch
blob with the fields below; cf. `ChainCorpus.__init__` at
`src/train_chain.py:970-1047`:

| field | shape / type | required? | source of truth | what it means |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `session_ids` | `(N_sessions, S)` int64 | **yes** | `tools/pretokenize_chains.py:202` | Pre-tokenised text, EOS-padded to `S=512` |
| `chain_starts` | `(N_chains,)` int64 | **yes** | same | Index of the first session row of each chain |
| `chain_lengths` | `(N_chains,)` int64 | **yes** | same | Number of sessions per chain (typ. 4-50) |
| `chain_names` | `list[str]` | **yes** | same | Used for source-bucket weighting (`longmemeval_…`, `msc_…`, etc.) |
| `session_len` | `int` | **yes** | same | Must equal the trainer's `--session_len` |
| `tokenizer` | `str` | **yes** | same | E.g. `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` |
| `session_callback_mask` | `(N_sessions, S)` int8 | **strongly recommended** | `tools/build_synthetic_persona_callback.py:484-505` | 1 on the *answer-span tokens* of the callback session; this is the supervision the +1.32-nat recipe uses (`--callback_loss_weight`) |
| `chain_callback_position` | `(N_chains,)` int64 | **strongly recommended** | same | Which session in the chain *is* the callback (sentinel `-1` = "no callback") |
| `chain_evidence_positions` | `list[list[int]]` | **strongly recommended** | same | Which sessions actually contain the answer (LongMemEval ships these as `answer_session_ids`); used by the curriculum sampler and the phase-aligned eval |
| `session_role` | `(N_sessions,)` int8 | optional (v16+) | same | 0=filler, 1=evidence, 2=callback |
| `session_evidence_mask` | `(N_sessions, S)` int8 | optional (v16+) | same | Per-token evidence-text mask |

The intermediate JSONL format that `pretokenize_chains.py` ingests
is *much* simpler — one row per session, schema either
`{"text": "..."}` or `{"turns": [{"speaker": "...", "text": "..."}, ...]}`
plus an optional `session_index`. The dialogue chain builder
(`tools/build_synthetic_dialogue_chains.py:76-109`) is the canonical
example. So the writer→trainer JSONL conversion is structurally
trivial; what is *not* trivial is the supervision (`*_callback_*`
fields), which has no analogue in the writer's data.

What the architecture actually consumes today is enumerated in
`paper_artifacts/chains/omni_memory_train_s512_manifest.json`:
21,378 chains, 269,538 sessions, 77,091 callback tokens — all
sourced from `lme_msc_train_s512.pt`, `synthd4v2_persona_callback`,
`synthd4_persona_callback`, and `synthd5_random_codes`. There is no
chain whose name begins `kurisu_…`, `linlu_…`, or any other writer
preset; `data_labeler_testing_env` is referenced in **zero** files
under `memory_residuals/src/`, `memory_residuals/tools/`, or
`memory_residuals/Scripts/`.

The thesis the data is supposed to serve is also worth restating
verbatim from `runs.md` so that the gap is concrete:

> "the next thing we're working on is making the model lean on
> **specific facts** stored in `M_c` (e.g. 'the user mentioned
> their sister's name was Marie three sessions ago') rather than
> the smoothed 'vibe of this conversation' posterior it currently
> relies on" — `runs.md:139-144`

That sentence is the bar the writer-produced data has to clear.
A chain in which Day N's dialogue *quotes a specific fact*
introduced in Day N-k (with k≥2), and whose tokens for that fact
in Day N are masked as the answer span, is exactly what
`synthd4v2_persona_callback` synthesizes today. The writer data
has the *first* property in part and the *second* property in
zero files.

## What the Writers Produce

A representative writer file is one JSON document per
(preset, user_id, dup_id, day_number). The schema, normalised
across the 775 Kurisu-CN and 38 Linlu-CN files I inspected, is:

```jsonc
// trimmed from presets_kurisu_CN/user_22_Day2_dup_1_simplified.json
{
  "user_schedule":      { "day": 2, "morning": "…", "noon": "…",
                          "afternoon": "…", "evening": "…", "night": "…" },
  "character_schedule": { "day": 2, "morning": "…", "noon": "…",
                          "afternoon": "…", "evening": "…", "night": "" },
  "history":   "在第一天的交流中，牧濑红莉栖和足利义咲从陌生开始…",
  "relationship": "两个人刚刚认识…",
  "intimacy_level":           0.35,
  "starting_intimacy_level":  0,
  "category":          "legacy_rejected",
  "rejection_reason":  "ai生成",
  "real_name":         "足利义咲",
  "dialogue": [
    { "content": "早上好",          "intimacy_delta": 0.005,
      "role": "User",   "timestamp": "09:30",
      "timestampManuallyEdited": true },
    { "content": "昨晚的论文看懂了吗", "intimacy_delta": 0.01,
      "role": "Kurisu", "timestamp": "09:32",
      "timestampManuallyEdited": true },
    // … typically 30–80 turns …
  ],
  // OPTIONAL on Kurisu, ABSENT on Linlu:
  "judgements": "...", "values": "...", "experiences": "...",
  "abilities": "...", "comments": [],
  "latest_ai_audit": { "overall_verdict": "passed|needs_improvement|rejected",
                       "rubric": { … 7 keys … }, "turn_issues": [...] }
}
```

The dialogue array is the primary payload. Each turn is
`{content, role, intimacy_delta}` plus optional `timestamp` /
`timestampManuallyEdited` / `reasoning_chain`. The
`reasoning_chain` field — which the audit rubric calls
load-bearing — is structured `[客观] ...\n[主观] ...` per
`writing_main.html:4222-4247`, but **is essentially never
present** (see finding (d) below).

Counts of Kurisu-CN files by category (auto-classified, n=775):

| category | count | what it means |
|---|---:|---|
| `legacy_rejected` | 433 | imported from old DB, marked rejected (often "ai生成") |
| `legacy_pending` | 194 | imported, never reviewed |
| `legacy_passed` | 108 | imported, marked passed |
| `legacy_legacy passed` / `legacy passed` | 20 | DB-migration artifacts, treat as legacy_passed |
| `(missing category field)` | 14 | mostly schedule-demo / fixture files |
| `passed` | 3 | reviewed under the new rubric (all `user_1000_*`, sample data) |
| `pending` | 1 | new-rubric pending |
| `in_works` | 1 | the rubric's reference-A fixture (`user_32_Day1_dup_2`) |
| `rejected` | 1 | new-rubric rejected |

Linlu-CN: 38 files, **all 38 have no `category` field at all** —
this character is essentially un-audited.

## Findings

### (a) Field-shape compatibility — *severity: BLOCKER for trainer ingest, SOLUBLE in principle*

Mapping each writer field to the trainer's expectation:

| writer field | trainer field | mapping | gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dialogue[].content` + `role` | session text inside `turns[]` | trivial: render as `"{role}: {content}\n"` per `pretokenize_chains.py:79-86` | clean |
| one Day file | one session | trivial: `session_index = day - 1` | requires deciding chain boundary (10 days = 1 chain? per-`dup_id`? per-user?) |
| `(preset, user_id, dup_id)` | one chain | trivial group-by | clean if you accept `dup_id` defines the chain |
| `character_schedule` (per-day) | nothing in trainer; in chat-time prompt | render-into-session vs. hold-out is a leak choice (see (e)) | **decision required** |
| `user_schedule` | nothing in trainer | same | same |
| `history` (LLM-generated summary of Day N-1) | nothing in trainer | this is exactly the "in-prompt summarizer" the architecture is trying to absorb (`runs.md:33-58`); must be excluded from chain text | **decision required** |
| `relationship` / `intimacy_level` | nothing in trainer | per-session bias if at all | nit |
| `reasoning_chain` (per-turn `[客观]/[主观]`) | nothing in trainer; arguably a slow-memory side channel | discussed in (d) | **medium opportunity** |
| `category` / `latest_ai_audit` | nothing in trainer | data-cleaning filter only | nit |
| ── *missing* ── | `session_callback_mask` | **NO source** in writer data | **BLOCKER** |
| ── *missing* ── | `chain_callback_position` | **NO source** | **BLOCKER** |
| ── *missing* ── | `chain_evidence_positions` | **NO source** | **BLOCKER** |
| ── *missing* ── | `session_role` | **NO source** | high serious |

A working converter (~150 LOC of Python) could in one afternoon
produce a `.pt` blob with the first six fields and zeroed
callback supervision. That blob would behave on the trainer
exactly like the `ultrachat_…` / `pippa_…` / `soda_…` chains
in the existing omni corpus: contiguous LM-NLL gradient with no
phase-aligned eval, no `--callback_loss_weight` benefit, and no
contribution to any pa_cb_dnm number. Per Prior #11, that is the
v24c regime that *goes negative* — adding it without callback
supervision would actively hurt the headline.

So the field-shape gap is real but small *for unsupervised
addition* and prohibitive *for headline-quality training*
without a separate annotator.

### (b) Callback density — *severity: SERIOUS, asymmetric across writers*

Sampling protocol: I read all 10 days of `user_22` (Kurisu CN,
mostly `legacy_rejected`) and `user_34` (Kurisu CN, runs
`legacy_passed` from Day 2 to Day 10), spot-read Linlu Day 1 +
Day 2, then ran a substring search for the 14 most common Chinese
callback markers (`昨天|昨晚|上次|前几天|之前你|之前我们|你说过|我记得|那天|那次|前天|你之前|上回|上周`)
across all 775 Kurisu-CN files. Hits in 125 / 775 = **16% of
files contain at least one callback-style phrase in the dialogue**;
note this both over- and under-counts (some "昨天" refer to
in-day morning-vs-evening, and many genuine callbacks use
phrasing like "你之前提到的那个X" that the regex misses, or simply
re-state a fact without a marker word).

Manual scoring on the user_22 / user_34 sample (Day N pairs with
N≥2) gives the impression below; small-sample, take rates with
salt:

| pair type | rate | example |
|---|---|---|
| **clean callback** (later day quotes a specific Day-N-k fact) | ~50 % of Day-N for N=2, dropping to ~15-25 % for N≥4 | user_22 Day 2 turn 1 (line 30) `"昨晚的论文看懂了吗"` ← Day 1 turn 60-67 (黑洞 paper); user_34 Day 2 turn 4 `"昨天和你说的那个喝多的稳定臂又抽风"` ← Day 1 character_schedule afternoon entry |
| **vibe-only continuity** (later day uses Day-N-k voice/topic but no specific fact) | ~30 % | user_34 Day 5 the entire 餐巾纸-inspiration thread; ties to Day 5 own character_schedule, not a Day 1-4 fact |
| **no callback at all** (self-contained day) | ~20-30 % | user_34 Day 6 (主管 / 异想天开 proposal — entirely Day-6 content); user_34 Day 9 mostly Day-9 content but contains *one* Day-1 callback `"伯克利下周会把新的控制板寄过来"` |

Three concrete examples (path:line):

> `presets_kurisu_CN/user_22_Day2_dup_1_simplified.json:30-43`
> `"昨晚的论文看懂了吗"` / `"看完了"` / `"但是基本没看懂"`
> — clean callback to Day 1's black-hole paper plotline at
> `user_22_Day1_dup_1_simplified.json:401-419` `"我在网上看到一篇关于黑洞的报道 / 然后顺着找到了相关的论文 / 打算熬夜看看"`. Day-2 also calls back via Kurisu's bedtime warning at line 499:
> `"别又熬夜看些看不懂的东西"`.

> `presets_kurisu_CN/user_34_Day2_dup_2_simplified.json:18-22`
> `"真是要死了）昨天和你说的那个喝多的稳定臂又抽风"` —
> direct verbatim callback to Day 1's stabilizer-arm content
> introduced via `character_schedule.afternoon`. Same file
> line 33-46 chains the Berkeley-control-board reveal, which is
> *itself* recalled at `user_34_Day9_dup_1_simplified.json:39-46`
> seven days later: `"是因为伯克利下周会把新的控制板寄过来"`.

> `presets_kurisu_CN/user_34_Day6_dup_1_simplified.json:14-50`
> opens with `"我今天差点和主管吵起来"` and stays inside
> Day 6's own character_schedule (异想天开 proposal). No reference
> to Days 1-5 at all. This is the "vibe-only / no-callback" pole
> of the distribution.

Punchline: **The writers are producing callbacks where they want to,
about 40-50% of the time on Day-2-after-Day-1 pairs**, but the
distribution is unconstrained. Cross-day callbacks at distance
k≥3 are rare (~10-20%) and never marked. The architecture's
training loss will see a noisy, unannotated gradient; the v18-v22
"the read-side gradient channel is missing under LM-NLL-only"
finding (Prior #10) is the relevant warning here.

### (c) Distractor coverage — *severity: NIT, accidentally fine*

Distractors (sessions with no callback) clearly exist (~20-30%
of mid-Days as scored in (b)). The corpus is not callback-saturated;
if anything it's the opposite. So the architecture would not
learn the trivial "always retrieve" policy from this data.

The catch is that distractors are *unmarked*. The trainer's
`session_role` field would need an annotator pass to pin which
sessions are evidence vs. distractor vs. callback. Without this,
the curriculum sampler (`chain_curriculum_window` at
`src/train_chain.py:1074-1099`) and the phase-aligned eval can't
construct `[evidence, distractor, callback]` windows, which is the
sampler that the v9-v11 corpus pivot was built around (see
`runs.md` v9c entry at line 425).

### (d) Reasoning-chain density — *severity: BLOCKER for the rubric, MEDIUM opportunity for training*

Quantitative result: across all 775 Kurisu-CN files,
`grep -l '"reasoning_chain"'` returns exactly **2** files:

```
presets_kurisu_CN/user_32_Day1_dup_13_simplified.json   (16 instances)
presets_kurisu_CN/user_1000_Day1_dup_0_simplified.json  ( 1 instance)
```

The first is the rubric's own gold-standard fixture (the Reference B
example pasted at `system_prompt.txt:128-213`). The second is in the
`user_1000_*` test-data block the user warned me about. Across the
38 Lin-Lu-CN files: zero. Across `presets_lin_lu/` and
`presets_kurisu/` (English): zero.

Net: the production data has reasoning_chain density ≈ 0 / dialogue-turn,
in spite of the audit rubric stating
"`reasoning_chain` present on most character turns […] **Zero
reasoning_chains = blocker**" (`system_prompt.txt:14`). Either:
- (i) the rubric is silently being applied only to *new* files
  (the 5 non-`legacy_*` Kurisu files), and the legacy mass is
  grandfathered, OR
- (ii) the rubric is being applied but writers consistently get
  `inner_thoughts.score: 1` (the worst score) and pass anyway on
  other criteria, OR
- (iii) the rubric is enforced by the AI auditor but writers are
  copy-pasting from old habits and the editor ignores it.

For the architecture, `reasoning_chain` is *structurally* what the
slow-memory channel wants: an explicit, per-turn "what does the
character know / believe / remember right now". If the writers
produced it, a converter could turn it into either (a) extra
session text appended to the dialogue (lossy: contaminates LM
loss), or (b) a parallel slow-memory token stream that gets
extracted into M_c separately (the cleaner option, but requires a
small architectural addition). At current density (~0%), neither
option is tractable.

The auto-fill heuristic at `writing_main.html:4163-4174`
(reasoning_chain auto-populated when content contains a hyperlink)
is a partial mitigation, but it only fires on URL-bearing turns
(rare).

### (e) Schedule-grounding leak — *severity: SERIOUS, by-construction*

`character_schedule` and `user_schedule` are stored in the writer
JSON and *also* served back to the chat client at inference time:
`internal/web/api.go:456-462` formats the schedule into a string
and serves it inside the writer file payload, and
`app.go:1186-1194` packages `ai_schedule` + `user_schedule` for
downstream consumption.

If a writer→trainer converter renders the schedule into the
session text at training time, the model has **the same
information at training time and at inference time**, regardless
of whether `M_c` is plumbed in or not. The "memory" channel's
nominal job — surfacing schedule-conditioned facts that aren't
in the prompt window — collapses to "echo the prompt", and the
+1.32-nat lift would be entirely explained by an in-prompt
schedule prior, not by the M_c primitive.

If the converter holds the schedule out of training-time chain
text but the inference pipeline still injects it, then training
and inference don't match: the trainer learns a memory writer over
schedule-free dialogue, and inference asks it to read against
schedule-laced context. That's the reverse of the v15b/v15f
joint-training leakage that Prior #9 flagged as a blocker.

The cleanest segregation, if any of this writer data is to be
trained on, is: **never include the schedule in training-time
chain text and never include it in the inference-time prompt
either; let the model learn to recover schedule-derived facts
from earlier dialogue alone.** That requires giving up the
labeler env's product behaviour (which leans on the schedule), so
this is an explicit fork-the-data-pipeline decision, not a
trivial flag flip.

The `history` field has the same character. It is an
LLM-generated summary of Day N-1, surfaced in the writer UI to
help the writer pick up where Day N-1 left off
(`writing_main.html:3380-3466`). If included in training-time
session text, it is precisely the "in-prompt summarizer" that
`runs.md:33-58` lists as one of the bolt-ons memory residuals
exists to absorb. It must be stripped before any chain build.

### (f) Voice-register drift on Linlu — *severity: NIT-to-CONCERN, separate from memory faithfulness*

The user explicitly raised this so I sampled. Canonical Linlu in
`writing_main.html:5575-5576` and the matching CN
`writing_main.html:5656` is "年轻的文学系老师" / "young
literature professor specializing in Tang/Song poetry, teaches
《中国古代文学史（唐宋卷）》". Sampling
`presets_lin_lu_CN/user_0_Day1_dup_1_simplified.json` (1300+ turn
chain) and `user_2_Day2_dup_1_simplified.json` (~2700 turns):

- Voice skews colloquial young-internet: `hhhh` / `好奸诈啊` /
  `【嘿嘿】` / `【过奖】` / `【侯明昊古风小生摇扇子】` /
  `余华不也会用这些字吗？我普普通通一个大学老师 对文学的追求再
  高能高得过余华吗？`. The user's in-fic "are you crafting a
  persona?" line at `user_0_Day1_dup_1_simplified.json:1212-1213`
  is itself a tell that the register is not landing.
- Specialised-knowledge content is sparse. Kurisu chains routinely
  carry physics shop talk that is *consistent with* her
  schedule (Higgs, stabilizer arm, Berkeley, control-board, the
  D-Higgs trap fluid, etc.). Linlu chains rarely cite Tang/Song
  literature, the《唐诗中的尘烟》book, or the historical-novel
  hobby that the canonical card lists.
- Voice quibble is independent of the user's "17-year-old vs
  professor" phrasing — the canonical age in the
  `new_user_info_lin_lu_cn.json` user records is 20-25 and most
  chats read as ~25; that's not the canonical character though.

This is real but orthogonal to memory-faithfulness. It would be a
problem for any character-fidelity downstream eval but does not
affect whether `M_c` can learn callbacks.

---

## Teaching-side recommendations (the user explicitly asked for this)

The user's framing — *"telling writers to add callbacks is a
teaching problem that needs to be fit into other parts of the
website"* — is correct. Each item below is a UI surface, not a
"please write better" rule. None of them are implementation; each
points at the file/template that would need to change.

1. **Callback Hint card on the Day-N writing page.** When
   `currentDayNum >= 2` and the writer opens a new dialogue, fetch
   Days 1..N-1 and surface 3-5 specific atom-facts ("you mentioned
   on Day 3 that your mother lives abroad", "on Day 5 you said the
   Berkeley control board hadn't arrived"). The fetch path already
   exists at `writing_main.html:3395-3404` (it's used by the
   history-generation button); the missing piece is a
   summarisation pass that emits *atomic claim-form* facts rather
   than the prose history field. The card would sit beside the
   `historyContent` div at line 3435 and persist while the writer
   is composing the dialogue.

2. **Callback rubric row in the AI auditor.** Add a
   `callback_density` row to the rubric table at
   `internal/web/audit_fixtures/system_prompt.txt:8-15`, scored
   1-5, defined as "fraction of character turns that quote, paraphrase,
   or otherwise functionally depend on a fact established in a
   prior day's dialogue / character_schedule entry". On Day 1
   the row is exempt. The rubric is what writers iterate against;
   making callbacks gradeable makes them learnable.

3. **Per-turn `reasoning_chain.[客观]` placeholder pre-filled with
   the Day-N-1 summary.** The objective-facts placeholder at
   `writing_main.html:4277-4279`
   (`"e.g. User and character had a great conversation last
   night, agreed to chat more"`) is a *callback example*. Rather
   than show it as placeholder text, pre-fill the textarea with
   the actual most-recent-prior-day summary the first time a
   character turn is opened, so the writer's default state is "I
   am writing a turn that is conditioned on what happened
   yesterday". This converts the missing-reasoning_chain blocker
   (finding (d)) and the missing-callback signal (finding (b))
   into the same UI fix.

4. **Guide / tutorial chapter on callbacks.** `templates/guide.html`
   currently contains a tutorial that walks writers through the
   schedule and intimacy fields but has no chapter on cross-day
   continuity (grep for "callback|previous|continuity|cross.day" in
   that file returns nothing relevant — only the dialogue-history
   panel internal to the demo). A worked example showing
   "Day N talks about pet dog → Day N+3 character asks 'how is
   the dog'" would set the expected baseline.

5. **Lounge / forum stickied "callback patterns" thread.**
   `templates/lounge.html` exists; a stickied thread that
   collects 5-10 examples of well-executed callbacks from
   `legacy_passed` files (e.g. user_34's stabilizer-arm and
   Berkeley arcs above) gives writers a concrete reference
   library. Cheap to author, valuable to retrieve.

6. **Pre-warm the new-day file with `history` auto-generated.**
   The history-generation button at `writing_main.html:3380-3466`
   is currently opt-in (writer must click it). Make Day-N (N≥2)
   files auto-trigger it on first open, the way
   `autoCopyProfileFromPreviousDay()` at line 9447-9523 already
   auto-copies profile fields. This makes the prior-day summary
   visible by default rather than something the writer has to
   summon.

7. **Move the `latest_ai_audit` rubric scores back to the writer
   in-line.** Today the AI audit is run server-side and the
   `latest_ai_audit` block ends up in the JSON, but the writer
   sees the result only on a separate review page. Showing the
   rubric scores live (especially after the new
   `callback_density` row) closes the feedback loop.

The teaching point is that none of these are "tell the writers
to add callbacks". They are *defaults*, *placeholders*, *example
libraries*, and *graded rubrics*. Per the user's framing, that's
the difference.

---

## Code-side recommendations

These are scoped to the writer→trainer pipeline gap and to the
two leaks. Diff sizes are rough.

1. **Build `tools/build_writer_preset_chains.py` in
   `memory_residuals_data/`.** Walk a preset directory, group
   files by `(preset, user_id, dup_id)`, sort by `Day` number,
   render dialogue rows as `"{role}: {content}"` per
   `pretokenize_chains.py:79-86` rules, hold out
   `character_schedule` / `user_schedule` / `history` from the
   chain text, emit the JSONL schema described in
   `build_synthetic_dialogue_chains.py:6-12`, then pretokenise.
   ~150 LOC, no callback supervision (so this stream behaves
   like the `synthdlg`/`pippa` buckets at training time —
   contiguous LM-NLL with no phase-aligned eval).

2. **Optional: companion annotator
   `tools/annotate_writer_callbacks.py`.** Take the JSONL output
   of (1), run an LLM pass per (Day N, Day k<N) pair, emit
   `chain_callback_position` and `chain_evidence_positions` at
   chain-build time. This is the only way to get the
   `--callback_loss_weight` recipe to fire on writer chains. ~250
   LOC + an LLM-call budget; quality cap is the auditor's
   discrimination on cross-day fact references.

3. **Pretokenizer assertion: schedule must not appear in chain
   text.** Add to `tools/pretokenize_chains.py` a defensive
   check that none of the rendered session strings contain the
   substrings stored in the source preset's `character_schedule`
   or `user_schedule` values. ~30 LOC, prevents the leak in
   finding (e) at build time.

4. **Source-bucket weight for `writer` in the omni recipe.** Add
   `"writer": 0.5` (small) to the `suggested_source_weights`
   block of
   `paper_artifacts/chains/omni_memory_train_s512_manifest.json`
   only after (1) lands and (2) is at acceptable quality. Until
   then, leave the writer chains out of the omni mix entirely,
   per Prior #11's "callback annotation density on the bulk of
   training chains is the dominant collapse cause" warning.

5. **Optional: a `reasoning_chain`-aware extract path.** If the
   reasoning-chain density problem (finding (d)) is fixed
   upstream, add an alternate extract source
   `--memres_extract_source reasoning_chain` to
   `src/train_chain.py:118-127` that reads the per-turn
   reasoning_chain text rather than the raw dialogue. ~80 LOC in
   `src/modeling_memres.py` to plumb through. This is an *Idea
   2* opportunity — explicit slow-memory side channel — that the
   v32-v34 sparse-writer wave has been chasing through synthetic
   means.

## Sample evidence

Inline quotations. Each prefixed with `path:line`.

> `src/train_chain.py:982-989` — the trainer is corpus-format
> agnostic *only* for unsupervised chains: "Existing
> pretokenize_chains.py output (PG-19/TV/MSC) lacks these; we
> fall back to an all-zeros callback mask […]".

> `tools/build_synthetic_persona_callback.py:20-27` — the
> reference closed-set callback structure: `EVIDENCE_1 …
> FILLER … EVIDENCE_2 … FILLER … CALLBACK "what was my favorite
> {color OR tool} again?"`. Writer data has nothing structurally
> equivalent.

> `paper_artifacts/chains/omni_memory_train_s512_manifest.json:12-49`
> — the active training corpus enumerates LME, MSC,
> synthd4_persona_callback, synthd4v2_persona_callback,
> synthd5_random_codes; **no writer-preset entry**.

> `runs.md:139-144` — "the next thing we're working on is making
> the model lean on **specific facts** stored in `M_c` (e.g.
> 'the user mentioned their sister's name was Marie three
> sessions ago')". The writer data could in principle deliver
> this; today it does not.

> `presets_kurisu_CN/user_34_Day2_dup_2_simplified.json:18-22`
> `"昨天和你说的那个喝多的稳定臂又抽风"` — clean Day-2 callback to
> Day-1 character_schedule.

> `presets_kurisu_CN/user_34_Day9_dup_1_simplified.json:39-46`
> `"是因为伯克利下周会把新的控制板寄过来"` — Day-9 callback to
> Day-1's Berkeley-control-board reveal (cross-day distance 8).
> This is the kind of distance-k callback that would actually
> stress-test M_c if it were labelled.

> `presets_kurisu_CN/user_34_Day6_dup_1_simplified.json:14-50`
> — Day 6 opens with "我今天差点和主管吵起来" and never references
> Days 1-5. Self-contained day; would be a distractor.

> `internal/web/audit_fixtures/system_prompt.txt:8-15` — the
> rubric does not score `callback_density` and lists
> `inner_thoughts` as a blocker if reasoning_chain is empty;
> `grep -c '"reasoning_chain"'` over the 775-file Kurisu CN
> corpus returns matches for **2 files**.

> `templates/writing_main.html:3380-3466` —
> `btnGenerateHistory.onclick` is the existing prev-day-summary
> path. It's *opt-in*; finding (b)'s callback gap could be
> partially closed by making it auto-trigger.

> `templates/writing_main.html:4277-4279` — the
> `reasoning_chain` objective-fact placeholder is itself a
> callback prompt: "User and character had a great conversation
> last night, agreed to chat more". Pre-filling this field
> instead of placeholder-displaying it is the smallest UI
> change that would directly produce callback signal.

## Open questions / unknowns

1. **What is the writer→memres pipeline supposed to be?**
   `memory_residuals_data/README.md` does not mention
   `data_labeler_testing_env` and no script in the memres repo
   references the labeler presets. It's possible the writers'
   work is *only* feeding the labeler's productized chatbot
   (`server.exe`/`server_sql.exe`) and was never intended to feed
   memres. If so, this audit is the right time to write that
   intent down explicitly, because the user's question implies
   they thought it *was* the training data. If the intent is
   *eventually*, the recommendations above are the path.

2. **Is the auditor rubric being enforced on legacy files?**
   The `legacy_*` category of 750+ files predates the rubric
   I read. I cannot tell from the JSON whether the
   `latest_ai_audit` block is being run retroactively or only
   on new submissions. Without that, the "0% reasoning_chain"
   number is harder to interpret.

3. **Server-side `/generate_history` prompt.** The endpoint is
   referenced at `writing_main.html:3421` and the Go server
   binary is compiled, so I can't see the exact prompt. If it
   summarises into a *prose* `history` field (current behaviour)
   vs an *atomic-fact-list* (what the callback-hint card in
   recommendation 1 needs), that's the load-bearing change for
   the teaching layer.

4. **Whether `M_c` should ever read the schedule directly.**
   Architecturally, the schedule is closer to a side channel like
   `reasoning_chain` than to a session of dialogue. If the writers
   are providing daily structured side data anyway, there may be
   value in feeding it into a *parallel* extract path (per
   recommendation 5) rather than into the dialogue stream — but
   that's an architectural question, not a writer-data question,
   and it's outside the scope of this audit.

5. **Whether the Linlu voice register issue is a writer-training
   problem or a character-card problem.** The canonical card
   describes Tang/Song-poetry teaching, but the
   `new_user_info_lin_lu_cn.json` partner profiles are 20-23
   year-old students/interns, which biases the conversation
   toward casual peer-to-peer texting. Fixing it may be a
   character-card revision rather than a writer-discipline issue.
